## Diagnosis (steps 1–2 — substrate + live reads)

**Substrate (as authored).** `POST /projects/:id/delete` stamps `projects.deleted_at` and sends
`project.purge` to pg-boss with `startAfterMs = +30 d`, `singletonKey = project.purge:<id>`
(`apps/api/src/project-routes.ts`); the api + worker both `createQueue('project.purge')` with
defaults; the worker's consumer re-reads `deleted_at` (restore ⇒ `restored` no-op; re-delete ⇒
`rescheduled` re-arm) and past grace hard-deletes the project tree + unreferenced object keys
(`apps/worker/src/jobs.ts`, `main.ts`). pg-boss is 12.30.0 (pinned).

**Live reads (2026-11-11T23:4xZ, prod).**

- Job `57bbef6f-bf5d-4f48-8f5b-1c7065aed5ff`: **0 rows** in `pgboss.job`/`job_common` by id AND by
  singleton key `project.purge:01M3SK38…` — absent in every state.
- Tombstone: **1 row** — `deleted_at=2026-09-30T21:41:10.945Z`, the ONLY `deleted_at is not null`
  project on prod; ≈11.1 d past its +30 d grace end (41.1 d tombstoned) at read time.
- `pgboss.queue` (`project.purge`): `policy=standard, retry_limit=2, retry_delay=0,
  expire_seconds=900, retention_seconds=1209600 (14 d), deletion_seconds=604800 (7 d)`,
  `updated_on=2026-09-25` (unchanged since before the job was armed 9-30).
- All 48 live `created` `project.purge` jobs carry `keep_until = start_after + 14 d`
  (`retention_seconds`) — so `57bbef6f`'s `keep_until` was **2026-11-13T21:41Z**, still in the future.
  The maintenance `deletion` clause (`state < 'active' AND keep_until < now()`) did NOT remove it —
  it went **terminal** (completed/failed/cancelled) on or before ~2026-11-04 and was pruned by
  `completed_on + deletion_seconds` (~+7 d ⇒ gone by ~11-06).
- Class repetition: the queue counts are 48 `created` + 3 `completed` — every past-grace tombstone
  in-window is accounted for (the surviving past-grace tombstone is unique ⇒ the class cannot be
  shown to repeat in-window; every OTHER tombstone's job is either pending correctly or its project
  was destroyed by the account pipeline first — the 11-03/11-05 `restored:true` no-ops).
- Cloud Logging (`rhema-prod-worker-cbdaf0f`, since 10-28): **zero** `[worker] project.purge` lines
  for `01M3SK38…`, **zero** `error` events (`jsonPayload.queue:*`), **zero** ERROR-severity lines,
  zero mentions of the job id. The worker was alive and polling at the fire instant
  (`billing.period-tick` 21:05Z, `billing.auto-reload` 21:20Z, `stripe.event` 22:23Z; the instance
  ran 10-30T19:29Z→10-31T16:33Z — no restart across the fire window).
- The project's content tree is intact (1 draft, 16 claims, 24 findings, 1 CI, 9 ROs/OFs, 1 run,
  25 artifacts) — consistent with the keyed `delete from projects` never having run.

**Root-cause class (what the evidence does and does not prove).**

- Ruled OUT: retention/expiry sweep (`keep_until` 11-13 in the future); deploy-window drop (worker up
  19:29Z→10-31T16:33Z, no restart at the fire instant; no pg-boss schema change in-window);
  dedup/singleton edge (`singletonKey` is inert under `standard` policy — the pg-boss 12 singleton
  unique indexes are all policy-gated — a second send never conflicts); fetch-side loss (fetch is a
  plain UPDATE); a code path calling cancel/deleteJob (none exists for `project.purge`).
- Ruled IN as a class: **an armed `project.purge` job can go terminal without ever executing and
  without any log or notice.** pg-boss 12's `#processJobs` swallows a handler throw — it calls
  `fail()` (retry → `failed` after `retry_limit=2`) and emits NO `error` event for handler failures;
  our work callback logs only *after* the handler returns. Best-supported mechanism: the worker
  fetched the job at 21:41Z, `handleProjectPurge` threw on all three attempts inside ~seconds
  (`retry_delay=0` ⇒ back-to-back; a transient pool/connection blip of that span suffices — the
  10-22 ECONNREFUSED window is the same ambient failure mode, though that one surfaced on the fetch
  path which DOES emit events) — `failed` ~21:42Z → pruned ~11-06T21:42Z. A raw/manual delete cannot
  be excluded from read-only evidence but has no supporting trace and no code path.
- The structural defect is identical under every candidate mechanism: **the 30-day purge contract
  is enforced only by the armed job itself — if it dies, nothing notices and nothing repairs.**

## Fix at source (step 3b — the class's loss path)

`apps/worker/src/jobs.ts` — **new `handleProjectPurgeSweep`** (the tombstone watchdog): scans
`projects` for tombstones older than 1 h lacking a live (`created`/`retry`/`active`) `project.purge`
job under `project.purge:<id>` and re-arms it at its own grace end (`startAfterMs =
max(0, deleted_at+30d−now)`; send failures never fail the sweep — the next hourly tick retries).

`apps/worker/src/main.ts` —
(a) the sweep rides the existing hourly `test-tenant.purge` tick (try/catch ⇒ `console.error`, never
fails the host job; logs `[worker] project.purge.sweep → …` only when it finds orphans);
(b) the `project.purge` consumer now wraps the handler in try/catch — a throw logs
`[worker] project.purge <id> FAILED …` BEFORE rethrowing, so pg-boss's retry/failure semantics stay
intact while the previously silent loss path becomes a log line.

`apps/worker/src/jobs.test.ts` — 7 focused tests (PGlite + a `pgboss.job` stub): past-grace re-arm
with `startAfterMs=0`; in-grace re-arm AT the grace end (~20 d); a live job in `created`/`retry`/
`active` suppresses the arm; a terminal (`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`) row does not; fresh
tombstones (<1 h) and live projects are skipped; the no-deps seam is a no-op. All pass (20/20 in the
file; 96/96 `apps/worker`).

## Survivor re-arm (step 3a — PROD WRITE, operator act)

`01M3SK380GQX41RKMD4KVFB34Q` remains tombstoned 11+ d past grace. Re-arm options, cheapest first:

1. **Deploy the fix (recommended)** — on the next worker deploy carrying this change, the hourly
   sweep detects the missing arm and sends `project.purge` with `startAfterMs=0`; the consumer fires
   on the next poll and destroys the project tree. Verify after deploy:
   `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="rhema-prod-worker-cbdaf0f" AND
   textPayload:"project.purge"' --freshness=3h` ⇒ expect
   `project.purge.sweep → {"scanned":1,"rearmed":["01M3SK38…"]}` then
   `project.purge 01M3SK38… → {"purged":true,"deleted":{…}}`; and
   `select id, deleted_at from projects where id='01M3SK380GQX41RKMD4KVFB34Q'` ⇒ 0 rows.
2. **Manual re-arm (if the purge is owed before a deploy)** — operator runbook: over the IAP tunnel
   with the system-role DSN, `INSERT INTO pgboss.job (name, data, start_after, singleton_key)
   VALUES ('project.purge', '{"tenantId":"01M2V3PM11XSF05VJ9G01PM5ZB",
   "projectId":"01M3SK380GQX41RKMD4KVFB34Q","tombstonedAt":"2026-09-30T21:41:10.945Z"}'::jsonb,
   now(), 'project.purge:01M3SK380GQX41RKMD4KVFB34Q')` — the worker's next poll fires it
   (`hand-date-tombstone.mjs`'s arm leg is the committed precedent for this shape). PROD WRITE —
   requires the operator's explicit go; not performed here.

## Dispositions this run

- **F-R6WATCH.2-1 / BL-112:** real loss, root-cause class identified and fixed at source
  (loud handler-failure log + self-healing re-arm sweep). The survivor's re-arm is dispositioned as
  the operator deploy/manual act above. BL-112's row lives on the `r6watch-2-reread` PR (#327); its
  close lands when that row merges + the survivor verifies gone — the fix and disposition are the
  `260_R6OPS.3` record. **Not closed here** — a past-grace tombstone still exists.
- **D-BL38.1-2 (CLK-1):** dated tail appended — criterion still UNMET (survives); row stays OPEN
  until the verify select returns zero rows; the fix + re-arm path is named.
- **GD-R6OPS.3-1** records the dispositions in LEDGER GATE DECISIONS.
- Judgement calls: (a) the sweep queries `pgboss.job` through the system pool — same audited seam
  `jobs.ts` already uses for `test-tenant.purge`/`account.hard-delete` (allowlisted in
  `tools/system-pool-boundary.json`); (b) `singletonKey` is kept on re-armed sends for convention
  even though it is inert under `standard` policy — the sweep's own `not exists` check is the real
  dedup; (c) the `<1 h` freshness margin avoids racing the api's own in-flight arm — a duplicate arm
  is benign regardless (second fire reads `restored:true`); (d) purge `del()` statements remain
  per-statement autocommits (unchanged — idempotent under retry; tightening to one tx is a separate
  reviewed change).
